At today's September event, Apple officially unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo, but did not announce the standard iPhone 18 at the same time. Here's why.

The standard iPhone 18 is expected to launch in early 2027, as Apple has adjusted its new product release schedule.

Generally speaking, today's Apple event would naturally be called the 'iPhone 18 launch event'.

However, Apple's arrangement caught many people off guard — they did not release the iPhone 18 today, at least not the standard version.

Apple only unveiled three premium new iPhones this time: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo.

This flagship lineup is clearly different from Apple's usual approach: in the past, new standard iPhones would be announced alongside the Pro models. However, back in May 2025, there were already reports foreshadowing this change.

According to multiple reports, the three new iPhones Apple launched today will be joined by three more new devices in early 2027:

  • iPhone 18
  • iPhone 18e
  • iPhone Air 2

So the standard iPhone 18 hasn't been cancelled — it's just shipping later than usual.

Why the change?

One explanation is that Apple wants to expand the iPhone product line with new models such as the foldable phone Duo, and doesn't want to launch too many products all at once in the autumn. Splitting the main iPhone launches into two cycles — autumn and spring — could be more advantageous.

Another possible reason is that Apple foresaw the current memory shortage early on, knowing that launching the standard iPhone 18 alongside the Pro and Duo models simultaneously would make it difficult to meet market demand.

Regardless, the iPhone 18 will eventually arrive — just not until early 2027.

What are your thoughts on Apple's strategy of splitting the iPhone 18 series launch into two phases? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
